title: Two Gaussians and a shared covariance
brief: Fit a Gaussian classifier by averaging, turn it into a logistic regression, then build both kinds of naive Bayes.
hints: The shared covariance divides by n, not by n - 1 or n - K. Add diff.T @ diff for every class into one (d, d) array, then divide once by n.

Factor once with L = cholesky(cov, lower=True). For each class, z = solve_triangular(L, (X - means[k]).T, lower=True) and np.sum(z**2, axis=0) gives the distance term. log det cov = 2 * np.sum(np.log(np.diag(L))).
gda_to_logistic only has to handle two classes. w = inv(cov) @ (means[1] - means[0]); b collects the two quadratic terms and the log prior ratio.
For the multinomial estimator, sum the count vectors of every document in a class before smoothing. Laplace smoothing adds alpha to every count and alpha * vocab_size to every denominator.
